title: Fixture manifest loader can fail with uncaught ValueError on Windows drive mismatches

finding.claim: Fixture manifest loader can fail with uncaught ValueError on Windows drive mismatches
finding.evidence: The containment check calls commonpath on 'full' and 'repo_abs' before handling path-root mismatches; on Windows, paths on different drives raise ValueError, which will surface as a generic load failure for valid-looking inputs.
finding.recommendation: Wrap the commonpath call in a try/except ValueError and convert it into the same explicit outside-repository error path used for other invalid manifest locations.

probe.summary: `probes/gap_commonpath_probe.py`, result `gap-commonpath-pair.txt`: - At HEAD, `_is_within` returns False (fails closed, no propagation) for inside/outside/mixed inputs, and under a monkeypatched `commonpath` that raises ValueError — the Windows cross-drive failure mode, simulated because real Windows drives cannot exist on this Linux host; the POSIX mixed absolute/relative case raises the same exception from the same call and is shown directly. - `_load_fixture_scope` against an outside-repo path produces the intended validation error ("resolves outside the repository"), not a raw commonpath traceback. - Git: at `4e5cbd8^` the loaders contain 2 direct unguarded commonpath containment checks and no helper; at `4e5cbd8` (v0.9.6) there are 0 and the helper exists.
